assessment.completionStatus: Successful — all 12 scenario steps executed and all 10 acceptance criteria were met. Both mock (--body) and abort routes worked on the first try and were cleanly reversible; HAR produced a valid 1.2 document containing both fixture URLs. However, several commands reported success without changing anything (unroute of a never-registered pattern, har stop with no recording), and the HAR/detail output silently omits response bodies for one of the fixture's two fetches, which is a data-quality gap in the headline feature.
assessment.successRate: 100% of steps and acceptance criteria completed as scripted; 0 blocking failures. Roughly 3 of 10 ACs were satisfied in a way that exposed defects (AC1 vs documented tracking lifecycle, AC5 body coverage, AC10 silent-success cases).
assessment.mostConfusingAspects: 1) The tracking lifecycle: the docs and help say tracking is lazy and starts on first use, but the first `network requests` call already returned traffic from a navigation that happened before any network command — a user cannot tell which model is true, or when the buffer started. 2) Silent-success semantics: `network unroute <pattern>` and `network har stop` both exit 0 while changing nothing (one of them even writes an entry-less .har). 3) Discoverability of state: there is no way to list active routes or to ask whether a HAR recording is running, and the advertised `--help --examples` path answers 'is the backend running?' on a perfectly healthy backend. 4) The `**` glob syntax is explained in `network route --help`, but the identical phrase 'plain text matches URLs containing it' next to 'glob supported' leaves the exact matching semantics (contains vs full glob) genuinely ambiguous — I confirmed behavior only by experiment.
assessment.mostValuableImprovements: 1) Make every state-changing network command report precisely what changed (route action + count, unroute removal count, cleared-entry count, recording state) instead of echoing the pattern. 2) Fix the HAR defects that make the artifact untrustworthy: 1000x timings, missing bodies for unconsumed fetches, and dropped spec fields. 3) Add read-only state commands: `network routes` and a `network har status` query. 4) Correct the tracking-lifecycle documentation (and the 'metadata-only entries' claim) so users can predict what the buffer contains. 5) Make `--help --examples` either deliver examples for the network family or stop blaming the backend. 6) A compact default listing for `network requests` (one line per request) would transform its usability on real pages.

issues.title: Response bodies are never captured for fetches whose body the page never reads (har --content text/all, network request)

sections.body:
1) Fresh session on http://localhost:18080/b4/network-fixture.html (its second fetch reads only `missing.status`, never the body).
2) ./b4w.ps1 -s S network requests --filter network-endpoint-ok -> note finished=false for the unconsumed one.
3) ./b4w.ps1 -s S network har start --content text; goto away/back; network har stop out.har -> entry for /api/network-endpoint-missing.json has content={size,mimeType} with NO text and time=-1.
4) ./b4w.ps1 -s S network request <id-of-missing> -> no responseBody field at all.
A/B control: eval --await --file with `fetch(url).then(r=>r.text())` vs `fetch(url).then(r=>r.status)` against the same URL -> finished=true vs finished=false, same encodedDataLength (173).
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The response body is captured (bytes were fully transferred, encodedDataLength=173), or the entry states why the body is unavailable (e.g. an _error/'body unavailable' note) instead of looking like a request still in flight.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Tracking entry keeps finished=false forever, timings.receive=-1, HAR time=-1, no body embedded under --content text (mime application/json qualifies), network request detail omits responseBody entirely, and no _error or note explains it. A 404 API call therefore appears bodiless and un-timed in the HAR.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Body capture (and the finished flag) is driven by the CDP Network.loadingFinished event. Chrome does not deliver loadingFinished for a fetch response whose body stream is never consumed/drained by page JS (observed: identical requests differ only by body consumption). NetworkObserver never marks such requests finished, so HarBuilder and networkRequestDetail skip body/timing. Inferred from A/B evidence and NetworkObserver.kt's loadingFinished-driven capture; confirm the exact Chrome event behavior for unconsumed streams.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-core/browser4-browser/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/chrome/network/NetworkObserver.kt (onLoadingFinished handler / harStop body drain); TrackedNetworkRequest.kt (finished, responseBodyBytes); browser4-core/browser4-browser/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/chrome/network/HarBuilder.kt:totalTimeMillis()
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Fall back to Network.getResponseBody for requests whose bytes arrived (encodedDataLength > 0) even when loadingFinished never fired, e.g. before building the HAR / answering a detail query.
- Mark such entries explicitly in tracking and HAR output (e.g. finished=false plus a bodyUnavailable reason) so consumers can distinguish 'no body' from 'still in flight'.
- Add an e2e fixture variant (or extend network-fixture.html) asserting the unread-body case, since the shipped fixture already hits it.
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: HAR entry timings are ~1000x too large (microseconds emitted where HAR 1.2 requires milliseconds)

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s S network har start --content text; ./b4w.ps1 -s S goto <url>; ./b4w.ps1 -s S network har stop out.har; then inspect an entry: e.g. entry 6 has time=11 but timings={send:196,wait:9173,receive:0}. sum(timings) ~ 600-900x the entry's own time for every entry.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: HAR 1.2 timings in milliseconds, consistent with the entry's total `time` (a localhost request that took ~11 ms should show wait ~9 ms, not 9173).
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: timings.wait/send values are 1000x the true duration; Chrome DevTools / HAR viewers display ~9 second waits for 8-11 ms localhost requests. timings.receive is consequently always 0 (clamped total minus inflated parts).
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: HarBuilder.deltaMillis() converts CDP timing offsets with (end-start)*1000, assuming seconds, while this Chrome build reports ResourceTiming offsets in milliseconds (the same file's totalTimeMillis converts the monotonic clock correctly, which is why `time` is right and `timings` are not). Inconsistency is provable internally: sum(timings) vs time.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-core/browser4-browser/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/chrome/network/HarBuilder.kt:buildTimings() and deltaMillis() (lines ~194-213 and ~331-334)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Fix the unit conversion in deltaMillis (drop the *1000 for ResourceTiming offsets, or scale from requestTime consistently), and add a unit test asserting sum(timings) is within a small tolerance of `time`.
- Derive `receive` from the monotonic total rather than a subtraction of possibly-clamped parts.
- Validate the produced HAR against the spec/DevTools import as part of the e2e suite.
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: network har stop succeeds silently when no recording is active (and writes an entry-less HAR file)

sections.body: After a previous har stop (no new har start): ./b4w.ps1 -s S network har stop -> prints a HAR document with no log.entries, exit 0. With a path: ./b4w.ps1 -s S network har stop out.har -> 'HAR saved to out.har (0 entries, content mode: text)', exit 0.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: An explicit 'no HAR recording is active' error or warning; nothing misleading is written or claimed. The documented contract ('the CLI only writes a file when the backend returned a real HAR document') should cover this case.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Silent success. The output document omits log.entries entirely (HAR 1.2 requires a `entries` array, which would be [] here), so it is not a valid HAR; the '(0 entries)' suffix is the only weak hint, and it is indistinguishable from a recording that legitimately captured nothing. There is also no command to query whether a recording is active.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: NetworkObserver.harStop() builds the HAR from the current buffer regardless of the harRecording flag and returns no recording-state error; the payload {recording=false,...} is not surfaced by the CLI. The empty entries list is then dropped in serialization (see the omitted-fields issue below).
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-core/browser4-browser/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/chrome/network/NetworkObserver.kt:harStop() (line ~301); cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:handle_har_stop()/parse_har_stop_payload()
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Have harStop() return an explicit 'no active recording' error (or a warning field the CLI prints) when harRecording == false.
- Include recording state in `network har stop` output; consider a `network har status`-style query so 'am I recording?' is answerable without stopping.
- Always emit log.entries (even empty) for spec-valid output.
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Documentation: 'tracking is opt-in and lazy ... traffic that happened before the first network command is not recorded' contradicts observed behavior

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s S open --headless http://localhost:18080/b4/network-fixture.html (fresh session); ./b4w.ps1 -s S network requests -> the very first network command already returns 4 entries, including the document request and both fetches from the navigation that preceded it.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Either the documented behavior (first call empty or containing only post-enable traffic; user re-navigates to populate), or documentation that matches reality (traffic is captured from the first navigation because the CDP Network domain is already enabled).
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The first call is fully populated with pre-command traffic. network.md (Quick Start + 'Errors & Recovery') and `network requests --help` ('Network tracking is enabled on first use') set the wrong expectation. The 'already-finished requests are kept as metadata-only entries' claim is also inaccurate: a pre-recording fetch entry was delivered with its body embedded.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The underlying Pulsar layer calls Network.enable during navigation setup (PulsarWebDriver.enableAPIAgents0() -> browserProtocol.networkEnable(); NetworkManager.enable()), so the Network domain is live before the CLI's first network command. NetworkObserver.ensureEnabled() is a second, lazy enable that only guarantees buffers/listeners; the docs describe only that layer. The 'metadata-only' wording ignores that bodies may still be retrievable from Chrome's buffers when the HAR is built.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: skills/browser4-cli/references/network.md (lines ~37-39 and ~197-199 'No requests tracked'); cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs `network requests` help text ('Network tracking is enabled on first use')
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Rewrite the tracking-lifecycle section to state that the Network domain may already be enabled by the browser layer, so requests from the current tab's earlier navigations can appear; keep 're-run the interaction' as a remedy only for evicted/rotated entries.
- Correct the metadata-only claim to 'bodies are embedded when still retrievable from the browser'.
- Make the buffered-entry cap/eviction behavior explicit (the 'bounded in-memory buffer' size is never stated).
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: --help <command> --examples is a documented dead end that misreports a healthy backend as down

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 network route --help --examples -> 'No examples available for 'network route' — is the backend running?' Direct probe: curl http://localhost:8282/mcp/tools/specs -> {"tools":[]}.

sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The advertised examples command yields nothing for all network commands, and the reason given wrongly blames the backend. Exit is still 0. A first-time user cannot tell whether the feature is missing, the backend is broken, or they typed it wrong.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: fetch_tool_spec_values_within() collapses every failure mode (connect error, non-JSON, empty list) into an empty Vec; build_tool_examples() maps 'specs.is_empty()' to 'is the backend running?'. The backend currently serves no tool specs at /mcp/tools/specs, so the message fires on every command even when healthy.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:build_tool_examples() and fetch_tool_spec_values_within() (lines ~20996-21015, ~21322-21340); backend endpoint /mcp/tools/specs serving {"tools":[]}
sections.label: Code Pointer

- Distinguish 'HTTP request failed' from 'server responded with zero specs' and word the latter as 'the backend advertises no tool examples'.
- Ship built-in examples for the network family (route/unroute/har are exactly the commands where the ** glob and --content modes need examples).

issues.title: HAR document drops spec-required/expected fields the builder populates (cache, cookies, queryString, redirectURL, page title, _error)

sections.body: Record a HAR and inspect: log.pages[0] has no `title`; entries have no `cache`; request objects have no `cookies`/`queryString` (even for URLs with a query); response objects have no `redirectURL`; no `_error` key on failures. HarBuilder.buildEntry() sets all of these (cache={}, cookies=[], redirectURL='', title='', _error='').
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: HAR 1.2 documents carry these keys (empty objects/arrays where nothing applies), which the docs also claim ('one entry per request with request/response/cache/timings ... and _error').
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The keys never appear in the emitted document, so the produced file is non-conformant for strict HAR consumers and the documentation overstates it.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Observed values are exactly the empty-string/empty-collection defaults, and the CLI was verified to pretty-print the backend payload verbatim (serde_json, no field filtering), so the strip happens backend-side in a Jackson/NON_EMPTY-style inclusion policy between HarBuilder and the HTTP response. The exact serialization hop still needs confirmation (none of the currently greppable mapper configurations obviously apply to this path).

sections.body: browser4-core/browser4-browser/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/chrome/network/HarBuilder.kt:buildEntry()/build() (values are produced here); serialization leaving values out is downstream (investigate the mapper used for the browser_har_stop tool result, e.g. MCPToolController / AgentToolManager result rendering)

issues.title: False 'Possible blocked/challenge page' warning fires on small but valid pages

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s S goto http://localhost:18080/b4/frame-other.html (a valid local fixture returning 200 with a heading, a button and a state div) -> stderr warning: 'Possible blocked/challenge page — detected page text is implausibly empty (50 chars) after a successful navigation.' Happened on both navigations to this fixture.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: No challenge warning for a plainly valid 200 response from a local server (the page text is intentionally short), or at least wording that does not suggest a block.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Two alarming warnings during a routine local test run; on a first-time user it reads like the tool is being blocked. The advice ('inspect with snapshot before escalating') sends users to investigate a non-problem.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The challenge probe's 'implausibly empty body' heuristic (visible character count with no iframes) has no baseline for intentionally small pages, and the warning text is framed as a possible block rather than a low-content note. SKILL.md itself calls this a weak signal, but the CLI message does not convey the low confidence.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:29246 (message 'page text is implausibly empty ... after a successful navigation') and the surrounding detection code (~29240-29510)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Soften the message for the weak signal and separate it from the strongly-named 'blocked/challenge' text (e.g. 'page has little visible text; if content is missing, inspect with snapshot').
- Skip or downgrade the warning for localhost/127.0.0.1 targets and for responses whose status and title look normal.
- Consider a content-length/body-size signal instead of only visible text length.
